To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PIM containing TBP as plasticizer and Cyanex-301 showed high transport efficiency of Am from 1 M nitric acid feed solution to 0.01 M EDTA strip solution and the membrane showed no significant loss of transport efficiency even after being exposed to a maximum gamma dose of ∼200 kGy.
the transport of Am3+ across PIMs is influenced by the choice of strip solution, carrier extractant and plasticizer.
the PIM containing Cyanex- 301 and NPOE as plasticizer is the most suitable for Am transport.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of Am(3+), a long-lived alpha emitter, transport from aqueous feed to a strip phase containing a complexing agent, and the effect of different parameters on the transport behaviour of this metal ion across a PIM.

the transport of Am3+ across CTA based PIMs containing Cyanex- 301 as the carrier extractants, the effect of varying Cyanex 301 and bipy concentration, the effect of complexing agents in the strip phase, the stability of the PIMs after gamma irradiation and the surface morphology of the PIM membranes.
the transport behaviour of Am3+ through polymer inclusion membranes (CTA) containing Cyanex 301 as the extractant and TBP or NPOE as the plasticizers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PIMs with Cyanex-301 are promising for Am transport.

the PIM containing Cyanex-3 as the extractant and tri-butyl phosphate (TBPO) or 2- nitrophenyloxy ethyl ether (NPOE), as the plasticizer, is the best membrane in terms of Am(3+ )selectivity and transport efficiency.
Cyanex-301 based PIMs are promising for the selective transport of Am(3+).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cyanex-301 is a good carrier for the selective Am transport and the PIMs containing Cyanex- 301 are stable against gamma radiation.

the PIMs containing Cyanex- 301 and TBP as the plasticizer is a good candidate for the transport of Am(3+), and the PIMs could be reused for at least ∼ 100 cycles without a significant decrease in the transport efficiency.

the Am3+ transport efficiency of Cyanex-301/TBP based membranes was higher than the Cyanex-301/NPOE based membranes, the back transport effect could be minimized by using EDTA as the complexing reagent in the strip phase, the Am3+ permeability was higher in the presence of higher Cyanex-301 concentrations and bipyridine concentrations and the membranes were stable to a gamma dose of ∼200 kGy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cyanex-301 based PIMs can selectively extract Am(3+) from a feed solution containing 1 M HNO3 and can be used as a potential candidate for the separation of Am(3+).
Cyanex-301 based PIMs are promising candidates for Am recovery from low level liquid waste.
PIMs can be used as an alternative to the liquid–liquid extraction process for Am separation from the spent nuclear fuel.
